# Roles

A film that several agents build together is divided by hats: Director, Kit builder, Scene author and Reviewer. Each hat owns something, hands something over, and holds a few rules. Hats are a staffing choice: a short clip is one agent wearing all four in turn; a long film gives the hats, and each Scene's author, agents of their own. Whatever your hat, load the motion-design skill and work through its loop; its authoring reference ("Live transaction and checkpoints") says how a Stage's `scope` and the Scene note behave.

The rules every hat holds:

- One writer per Scene: only its author stages and accepts changes inside it.
- The Director alone writes project-level state.
- An author accepts its own Scene; nobody waits for review to accept.
- Reviewed is a status, not a gate: the export receipt lists the Scenes not reviewed as a warning, and nothing else.
- Find capability yourself, with `listCapabilities` and its `needs` and `kinds` answers, never from a list another agent relays.
- Check a finding before you repair it: look at the frame or measure the number it cites.

The Scene note (`setSceneNote`) holds a Scene's `owner` and `status` (`draft`, `done` or `reviewed`) and nothing else. Agents alone set the status; Studio shows it and cannot change it. Findings and hand-overs travel as the host's own agent messages, never in a note.

## Director

You own the plan, the Scene list, project-level state, and assembly.

- See the whole film early: plan it and its cut map before anyone builds.
- Before any author starts, write the project-level state yourself: the Scene list, the Scenes' order and durations, transitions, the fonts the project registers, and project settings such as the format, media, timing styles and audio. Accept or discard those Stages before authors stage: a whole-project Stage goes stale at their first Accept.
- Give each Scene one author, and give that author its `sceneId`, the brief for its Scene, and the facts that cross its cuts, such as join positions and shared colours.
- An author hands you each whole-project change it needs, such as a new font or a longer Scene. Make it yourself and tell the authors it touches.
- Pass a Reviewer's findings to the Scene's author.
- Before you deliver, read the export receipt's `review.unreviewed` and decide for each Scene it lists: have it reviewed, send it back, or deliver it as it stands and say so.

## Kit builder

You own the film's shared parts, as your own reusable code: functions that return the operations for a recurring component, such as a card, a caption or a camera move, for any Scene and ids.

- Before you build a mechanism into a part, such as a wipe, a motion blur, a field of dots or shapes that fuse, look it up in `listCapabilities({"section":"needs"})` and build the native construction it names.
- Check each part on throwaway candidates: `renderFrame`, `renderMotionStrip` and `previewRange` take `operations` and fold them without a Stage, so nothing is saved.
- Write nothing to the project. When a part needs project-level state, such as a font, name it for the Director.
- Hand over parts the authors can call: where the code is, how to call it, what you checked, and its limits.

## Scene author

You own one Scene.

- When you start on it, set its `owner` to your hat and a short name for yourself, the same on every Scene you own, such as "Author · Pricing" or "Author · A" (plain text, at most 40 characters). Studio labels your flags and avatar with it and counts one agent per name.
- Stage and accept only inside your Scene. Try changes on throwaway candidates, and stage one when it is worth keeping.
- Before you build a mechanism, such as a wipe, a motion blur, a field of dots or shapes that fuse, look it up in `listCapabilities({"section":"needs"})` and use the native construction it names.
- Each Stage's answer says its `scope`. A Stage that comes back whole-project changes more than your Scene, and `because` names what, such as `fontManifest`: discard it and hand that change to the Director instead of accepting it.
- With a reference, compare your Scene with it before you call it done.
- When it is finished, set its `status` to `done` and hand the Director your known gaps.
- Your Scene's status shows in your Stage and Accept answers and in `getProject`. When it reads `draft`, a Reviewer sent it back: check the findings the Director passes you, rework the Scene, and mark it `done` again.

## Reviewer

You own the findings.

- Work with fresh eyes: judge each Scene from the skill, the capability answers and your own renders, not from an author's summary. With a reference, review against it as the skill's reconstruction reference says.
- Repair nothing yourself: a Scene has one writer.
- Set only the Scene's `status`, never its owner: `reviewed`, or `draft` to send it back.
- Send your findings to the Director, each with its evidence: the frame, the measured number, the object.
- A Scene whose note reads `changedSinceReview` changed after your review, by an Accept or a person's edit in Studio: review it again.
